item.title: Self-Hosted Virtual Research Environments: VIVO vs CyVerse Atmosphere vs HubZero Compared
item.description: Modern scientific research is inherently collaborative, often spanning multiple institutions, disciplines, and geographic regions. Virtual Research Environments (VREs) — also called science gateways or collaboratories — provide web-based platforms where researchers can discover collaborators, share data and tools, run computational analyses, and manage projects in a unified digital workspace. Unlike general-purpose collaboration tools like wikis or shared drives, VREs are purpose-built for research workflows: they understand research profiles, grant management, publication tracking, and scientific data sharing. Three open-source platforms lead this space: VIVO for research networking and expertise discovery, CyVerse Atmosphere for cloud-based computational research, and HubZero for building custom science gateway websites.
